newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt, Kuwait, Lebanon clearing firms sign deal.
newsitem.headline: Egypt, Kuwait, Lebanon clearing firms sign deal.

text.p: The companies that handle clearing and settlement for the stock exchanges in Egypt, Lebanon and Kuwait on Thursday signed a cooperation agreement described as a landmark on the road to an Arab common market.
Under the agreement, Misr Clearing Co of Egypt, Midclear of Lebanon and the Kuwaiti Clearing Co will work together when the three exchanges start cross-listing shares, possibly next year.
Company officials said it was a practical follow-up measure to the cross-listing agreement the three exchange authorities signed in Beirut a month ago.

But, meanwhile, Lebanese who want to buy Egyptian shares, for example, can do so only though their local broker's partner broker on the Egyptian exchange and it is the Egyptian clearing company that will settle the transaction.

Ali Nigm, chairman of Misr Clearing Co, told the signing ceremony that an Arab common market could come about only though cooperation between capital markets and the new agreement was an important step in that direction.
"We have the resources, we have the trained personnel, all we need is the organisation and the cooperation," he added.

The Egyptian exchange had rushed through its new clearing and settlement system to ensure it was up and running in time for the ceremony. Brokers have been complaining of troubles with the system most of this month.

The director general of the Kuwaiti Stock Exchange, Hisham al-Oteibi, said he hoped the Kuwaiti parliament would soon remove restrictions on non-Kuwaitis owning Kuwaiti stock, clearing another obstacle to a regional capital market.
Nigm signed the agreement with Asaad Sawaya, the chairman of the Lebanese company, and Mashari al-Khaled, the chairman of the Kuwaiti company.
